opportunities.title: Google Earth Engine Noncommercial Partner Tier (100,000 EECU-hours/month for climate & nature projects)
opportunities.program: Earth Engine noncommercial quota tiers (Community / Contributor / Partner)
opportunities.deadline_text: No deadline. Tier can be changed at any time; Partner Tier 'Requires a separate application with details about your project and its impact.' Noncommercial status reverified annually and Partner Tier projects must reapply each year.
opportunities.funding_text: In-kind compute quota: Community 150 EECU-hours/month (default); Contributor 1,000 EECU-hours/month (requires active billing account, noncommercial usage not charged); Partner 100,000 EECU-hours/month (by application). Quotas enforced for noncommercial projects since 2026-04-27; exceeding quota puts the project in restricted (slower) mode.
opportunities.eligible_applicants: Registered noncommercial Earth Engine projects. Partner Tier aimed at nonprofits/NGOs, university and government research groups and similar organizations with heavy compute needs and clear evidence of high-impact sustainability work; priority to groups under a single PI.
opportunities.cgiar_eligibility_notes: CIAT/Alliance qualifies for noncommercial use as a nonprofit research organization ('Earth Engine will remain free of charge for nonprofit organizations using the services for scientific research'). Apply as lead for a lab/team-level Partner Tier project (one project per group; splitting requests across projects is a ToS violation).
opportunities.lead_applicant_requirements: Project must already be registered as noncommercial; real identity and organizational email; one application per lab/organization group (no quota farming).
opportunities.cofunding_details: Contributor tier needs a Cloud billing account attached, but noncommercial Earth Engine usage is not charged.
opportunities.eligible_activities: Projects related to climate mitigation, adaptation (climate change resilience), or protection (nature and biodiversity protection, management and restoration).
opportunities.required_documents: Online application describing the project, its compute needs and its climate/nature impact (form via Earth Engine help page).
opportunities.application_procedure: 1) Register Cloud project for noncommercial Earth Engine use; 2) move to Contributor tier on the Manage Tier page (immediate); 3) for Partner Tier submit the separate application via developers.google.com/earth-engine/help#computational_tiers; decision 'within several weeks'.
opportunities.scientific_alignment_rationale: Core infrastructure for the team's Sentinel/Landsat/MODIS crop and landscape analytics, AlphaEarth satellite embeddings (public in EE catalog) and yield/phenology mapping at scale.
opportunities.strategic_relevance_rationale: Since quotas started (April 2026) default 150 EECU-h/month is a real bottleneck for regional/continental CIAT products in LAC/Africa/Asia; Partner Tier secures free compute for a year.
opportunities.technical_feasibility_rationale: Team already uses Earth Engine daily; application is lightweight.
opportunities.recommendation: Pursue immediately. Highest-value, low-effort item in this group. Consolidate Alliance climate/landscape EE workloads under one PI-led Partner Tier project.
opportunities.potential_partners: Internal Alliance Climate Action / Multifunctional Landscapes teams; Google Earth Engine partner team.
opportunities.next_action: Check current tier of the team's EE Cloud project(s); switch to Contributor now; draft Partner Tier application (project description, expected EECU usage, climate adaptation/nature impact evidence, publications).

evidence.deadline_quote: Partner Tier: 'Requires a separate application with details about your project and its impact.' ... 'We'll review your application and get back to you with a decision within several weeks.'
evidence.eligibility_quote: Earth Engine will remain free of charge for nonprofit organizations using the services for scientific research. Partner Tier: projects related to climate mitigation, adaptation, or protection; aimed at nonprofits/NGOs, university research groups, government research groups ... with 'clear evidence of high-impact sustainability work.'
evidence.status_quote: Since April 27, 2026, noncommercial projects have a monthly EECU-hour quota ... You can change a project's tier at any time.

opportunities.title: Google Cloud Research Credits (academic research grants)
opportunities.program: Google for Education - Google Cloud research credits
opportunities.deadline_text: No deadline stated on the page; online application form available. Credits must be activated within 60 days of the project start date; credits expire 365 days after redemption.
opportunities.funding_text: Google Cloud credits; amount not stated on the official page (form asks for expected costs from the GCP pricing calculator). Third-party mirrors cite up to USD 5,000 for faculty/postdocs (not confirmed officially).
opportunities.duration: Up to 12 months (credit expires 365 days after redemption or when used up)
opportunities.eligible_applicants: Faculty, PhD students and postdoctoral researchers at accredited higher education institutions and eligible nonprofit research institutions in approved countries.
opportunities.eligible_countries: Approved country list on the page; Colombia is listed.
opportunities.cgiar_eligibility_notes: Form offers institution type 'Nonprofit Research Institution' and Colombia is an approved country, so CIAT staff (PhD-level researcher) can apply as lead; 'eligible' nonprofit research institution is not defined, so final eligibility is at Google's discretion.
opportunities.lead_applicant_requirements: Faculty / postdoc / PhD student at an eligible institution; institutional email preferred; Google Cloud Billing Account ID required.
opportunities.cofunding_details: Form asks how the project will be funded after credits expire.
opportunities.eligible_activities: Non-commercial research on Google Cloud (compute, storage, Vertex AI etc.).
opportunities.required_documents: Online form: personal/institutional details; project name and start date; proposal of max 250 words (research problem, GCP tools, timeline, milestones, outcomes, future GCP support); field of research; external funding; pricing calculator estimate + URL; Cloud Billing Account ID.
opportunities.application_procedure: Complete the online form on the official page.
opportunities.scientific_alignment_rationale: Useful for training EO/foundation models and running crop-model ensembles on GCP close to Earth Engine data; generic compute support.
opportunities.strategic_relevance_rationale: Small, one-off in-kind support; complements EE Partner Tier.
opportunities.recommendation: Apply for a defined project (e.g., fine-tuning AlphaEarth embeddings / yield forecasting for Honduras or SAI crop impact runs). Low effort, modest return.
opportunities.next_action: Prepare pricing-calculator estimate and 250-word proposal; create billing account; submit form.

opportunities.title: AWS Cloud Credit for Research
opportunities.program: AWS Cloud Credit for Research (also the route used by Amazon Sustainability Data Initiative for researcher credits)
opportunities.deadline_text: Proposals are evaluated 'on a rolling basis throughout the year.' Typical review 90-120 days.
opportunities.funding_text: AWS Promotional Credit. 'Student awards will be up to a maximum of $5,000.00.' 'Faculty and Staff awards are not capped.' EC2 limited to on-demand and spot instances.
opportunities.eligible_applicants: Full-time faculty, full-time research staff, and graduate/post-graduate/PhD students at an accredited research institution.
opportunities.eligible_countries: Not specified on the official page
opportunities.cgiar_eligibility_notes: CIAT staff are full-time research staff at a research institution, but 'accredited research institution' is not defined; CIAT is not an academic institution. Apply as lead and state CGIAR status; fallback is via a university partner.
opportunities.lead_applicant_requirements: Full-time faculty/research staff at an accredited research institution.
opportunities.eligible_activities: Per program description: building publicly available cloud-hosted science tools, proof-of-concept/benchmarking of moving research workloads to the cloud, training the community via workshops/tutorials.
opportunities.required_documents: Not specified on the main page (see FAQs and Terms linked from it).
opportunities.application_procedure: 'Apply now' link on the official page; communication via aws-research-credit@amazon.com.
opportunities.scientific_alignment_rationale: Generic compute; relevant if building open cloud-hosted tools (e.g., crop model/advisory APIs, Sentinel data on AWS Open Data).
opportunities.strategic_relevance_rationale: Uncapped staff awards could support an open-source climate data infrastructure product.
opportunities.recommendation: Apply only if a concrete AWS-hosted public tool is planned (e.g., open crop-forecast service using Sentinel-2/ERA5 on AWS Open Data). Otherwise prioritize Google credits.
opportunities.potential_partners: Optional university co-PI to remove accreditation ambiguity.
opportunities.next_action: Read AWS research credits FAQ/T&Cs to confirm whether non-university research institutes qualify; scope a public tool proposal.

evidence.deadline_quote: evaluated on a rolling basis throughout the year
evidence.eligibility_quote: Full-time faculty at an accredited research institution; Full-time research staff at an accredited research institution; Graduate, post-graduate, or PhD students enrolled at an accredited research institution

opportunities.title: Anthropic AI for Science program (free Claude API credits)
opportunities.deadline_text: No deadline; application form states submissions are evaluated monthly.
opportunities.funding_text: 'significant API credits to qualified researchers' - amount not specified.
opportunities.eligible_applicants: 'Researchers attached to a research institution'; form: qualified nonprofit and academic researchers.
opportunities.cgiar_eligibility_notes: CIAT researcher can apply directly as lead (nonprofit research institution). Program explicitly cites 'Increasing agricultural productivity' as an example application.
opportunities.lead_applicant_requirements: Researcher attached to a research institution; academic/institutional email and credentials preferred.
opportunities.geographic_restrictions: Not specified (presumably Anthropic-supported countries; Colombia is generally supported - not confirmed on page)
opportunities.eligible_activities: Research where AI accelerates science; 'particular focus on biology and life sciences applications', incl. 'Increasing agricultural productivity'; also welcomes natural sciences and math.
opportunities.required_documents: Online Google Form (3 pages; contents of pages 2-3 not visible).
opportunities.application_procedure: Submit the application form; reviewed monthly by Anthropic team incl. subject matter experts; unsuccessful applicants not notified individually.
opportunities.scientific_alignment_rationale: Agriculture explicitly in scope; useful for LLM-based agro-climatic advisory, literature/data mining, agentic coding for crop-model/EO pipelines; not EO-specific.
opportunities.strategic_relevance_rationale: Low-cost enabler for digital advisory tools and research software; small scale.
opportunities.technical_feasibility_rationale: Short form; team already does Python/ML.
opportunities.recommendation: Apply with a focused agriculture use case (e.g., LLM-assisted climate advisory for smallholders in Honduras/Colombia, or automated extraction of crop-trial data). Low effort.
opportunities.next_action: Fill the form with a concrete project and expected token usage.

opportunities.title: Google Earth Noncommercial Credit Program (credits for Google Earth Professional / Professional Advanced plans)
opportunities.program: Google Earth Public Programs - Noncommercial credits
opportunities.funding_text: Credits to cover monthly subscription costs of Google Earth Professional and Professional Advanced plans (amount not stated).
opportunities.eligible_applicants: 'Only nonprofits, crisis response organizations, news media organizations' and faculty at educational organizations.
opportunities.cgiar_eligibility_notes: CIAT would apply as a nonprofit organization; detailed criteria are on the Public Programs page (not loaded).
opportunities.lead_applicant_requirements: Nonprofit status; Cloud billing account linked to Google Earth.
opportunities.cofunding_details: Free trial requires a payment method, then upgrade to paid billing account before credits apply.
opportunities.eligible_activities: Projects on climate change mitigation, adaptation, protection or public health with 'clear evidence of high-impact sustainability or public health work.'
opportunities.required_documents: Public Programs form + reply to support ticket explaining which features/data layers/scale need a Professional plan.
opportunities.application_procedure: Start Professional trial -> upgrade billing -> Public Programs page -> select org type -> form -> support ticket follow-up.
opportunities.scientific_alignment_rationale: Google Earth Professional (incl. Gemini/AI features) useful for landscape stakeholder work; less central than Earth Engine.
opportunities.recommendation: Optional; pursue only if the team needs Google Earth Professional features for landscape engagement.
opportunities.next_action: Review Public Programs eligibility page; decide need.
